Chapter 6: The Deepening of Faith and the Challenge of Surrender
There comes a point in every journey when curiosity just isn’t enough anymore. The road ahead begins to ask something deeper—it asks for trust.
For our young man, standing right at the edge of adulthood, faith is shifting. It’s not just an idea to be tossed around or a childhood memory he looks back on. Now, it’s something real, something that actually demands an answer from him. It’s about surrender—not just of the mind, but of the will.
He’s surrounded by friends who, each in their own quiet way, live out a faith that’s both thoughtful and brave. Are their lives perfect? Not at all. But there’s a kind of steadiness about them—a purpose that’s hard to miss. He sees them wrestling with their own doubts, getting hit by disappointments, yet still choosing to believe.
It isn’t blind faith, either. What he witnesses is a hope that sticks around even when the answers don’t show up.
One evening, after a long walk with a friend, the young man really feels the weight of his resistance. He’s spent years building up walls of skepticism, but lately, those walls feel less like safety and more like a prison. That longing for joy, which used to be just a distant ache, is now a steady presence in his life.
It’s almost as if something—or maybe someone—is quietly, but persistently knocking at the door of his heart.
He tries to reason his way out, searching for some loophole that lets him stay in control. But those arguments, once so convincing, now feel thin and flimsy.
He realizes there are mysteries in this world—like the beauty of a sunrise, the ache we feel listening to music, or the pull of a true friendship—that can’t be boxed in by logic alone. These moments point to something bigger than just facts and figures.
Let’s be honest—surrender doesn’t come easily. There are nights spent pacing the floor, silent prayers that sound more like arguments, and long moments wrestling with himself. But bit by bit, almost without realizing it, his defenses start to crumble.
He starts to see that faith isn’t about having every answer. It’s about choosing to trust, even when things don’t make sense. It’s about saying yes to the idea that maybe, just maybe, this longing for joy is a real invitation—not some cruel joke.
Most of us, when we’re faced with the challenge of surrender, hesitate. Letting go of control? That’s tough. Admitting we don’t have it all figured out? Even tougher.
But for our young man, this moment of surrender isn’t some dramatic leap—it’s more like a gentle yielding. A quiet acceptance that he’s not alone, and that the longing he feels points to something true.
Looking back, he can see that this surrender isn’t really the end of his journey. In fact, it’s the start of something new.
The questions are still there, but now they’re held in the light of hope. And that search for joy? It’s no longer a lonely quest. Now, he shares the path with others, walking together toward something real.
